title: L&T Wins Third Ultra-Mega Middle East Gas Project Worth Over 15,000 Crore in August
excerpt: The gas compression contract is Larsen and Toubro's third order exceeding 15,000 crore rupees this month, reinforcing the Indian engineering giant's dominance in Gulf energy infrastructure.
body:
• Larsen and Toubro has signed a contract for an ultra-mega gas compression project in the Middle East, valued at over 15,000 crore rupees (approximately $1.8 billion).
  • This is L&T's third ultra-mega order in August 2026 alone, underscoring the company's dominance in global energy infrastructure.
  • The contract was awarded to L&T Energy Hydrocarbon (LTEH), which has over three decades of experience in upstream, midstream, and downstream EPC projects.
  • L&T shares have responded positively to the announcement, with the stock rising on the news.

L&T Lands Another Mega Energy Contract

Larsen and Toubro has secured yet another ultra-mega contract in the Middle East, this time for a gas compression project valued at over 15,000 crore rupees, the company announced on Saturday. It is L&T's third contract carrying the ultra-mega designation — reserved for orders exceeding 15,000 crore rupees — in August 2026 alone, according to CNBC TV18.

The contract was awarded to L&T Energy Hydrocarbon (LTEH), the company's hydrocarbon arm, which will handle the engineering, procurement, and construction of gas compression facilities in the region. The specific client and country were not disclosed in the exchange filing, consistent with L&T's standard practice for Middle Eastern contracts.

A Pattern of Record-Breaking Orders

The latest win adds to what has been an extraordinary August for L&T's order book. Earlier this year, the company secured its single-largest contract ever — the COMP4 package of QatarEnergy LNG's North Field Production Sustainability project, valued between $4 billion and $5 billion according to MEED. That deal involved the engineering, procurement, fabrication, installation, and commissioning of two offshore compression complexes located approximately 80 kilometers off the northeast coast of Qatar.

In October 2025, LTEH won another ultra-mega order for a natural gas liquids (NGL) plant in the Middle East, in consortium with Greece-based Consolidated Contractors Group. That project involved processing rich associated gas to produce lean sales gas, ethane, propane, butane, and hydrocarbon condensate.

"The ultra-mega order reaffirms L&T's position as a trusted partner in delivering mega energy infrastructure. It underscores our growing global footprint and ability to execute projects of high complexity."

— S.N. Subrahmanyan, Chairman and Managing Director, L&T

India's Growing Energy Infrastructure Footprint

L&T's string of Middle Eastern mega-contracts reflects India's expanding role in global energy infrastructure. The company's hydrocarbon division has built a track record across refinery expansions, petrochemical complexes, gas processing plants, fertilizer units, LNG terminals, and cross-country pipelines, making it one of the few Indian EPC firms capable of competing for contracts at this scale.

The Middle East's energy infrastructure investment cycle has accelerated in recent years, driven by Gulf states' push to expand LNG production capacity and diversify their hydrocarbon processing operations. Qatar alone is investing tens of billions of dollars in expanding the North Field, which holds recoverable reserves exceeding 900 trillion standard cubic feet — roughly 10 percent of the world's known natural gas reserves.

Market Reaction and Outlook

L&T shares have responded positively to the sustained flow of ultra-mega orders. Analysts at Axis Capital noted earlier this year that L&T was on track to comfortably surpass its consolidated order inflow guidance of 10 percent year-on-year growth, with international orders accounting for more than half of total inflows.

For investors tracking Indian companies with global infrastructure exposure, L&T's hydrocarbon division has emerged as a bellwether for Middle Eastern energy spending. The company reported a 14 percent increase in consolidated net profit and a 17 percent jump in revenue from operations in its most recent quarterly results.

With three ultra-mega orders in a single month, L&T's energy business is operating at a pace that even its own management would have considered exceptional just two years ago.
